notes.title: The Community Update (1.2) - Dev Diary
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!! The next big update for Carnaval Simulator is almost here: [b]The Community Update[/b] (1.2). This update is packed with new features, improvements, and fun additions to enhance the game's possibilities. As always, we value the input from our amazing community, so keep those suggestions coming on [url=https://discord.gg/vZbVsU5XMS]Discord[/url]! Now, let’s dive into the exciting features coming your way in this update.

[h1]Enhanced Visitor Interactions[/h1]
1 of the biggest most exciting new features is the enhanced visitor interactions. Visitors can now engage in small talk, discuss the location, comment on the music, and even complain about the weather. They can also give compliments or criticize your float, talk about construction clubs, power outages, and much more. These dynamic conversations bring the parade to life and make the game more engaging than ever before.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/27bf249ca86d745e7401bd8e4624abd93aa85294.png[/img]

[h1]Barrier Feature[/h1]
When a lot of visitors come to watch your parade, barriers will automatically appear to manage the crowd. This feature adds to the realism and helps control the flow of spectators.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/0db0a286d0fcd2f5a0ccd4c01ec0a733faa7ff3e.png[/img]

[h1]Standalone Tractors[/h1]
Introducing the Standalone Tractor! Now, you can have your tractor float without needing to attach other carts. This gives you more flexibility and creativity in your parade designs. Experiment with different setups and see what works best for your vision.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/2bf0f1b687daa45d806cf09af2db50cd9d301253.png[/img]

To help you get started with the new Standalone Tractor feature, we’ve added a dedicated campaign level. This level will guide you through all the possibilities and nuances of using a standalone tractor, making sure you get the most out of this new feature.

Additionally, we’ve introduced a possible new trait for your floats: the Frontal Cart AI Preference. This trait gives more points for well-decorated tractors, encouraging you to put more effort into making the front of your float as impressive as possible.

[h1]Pop Up System[/h1]
Our new Pop Up System will keep you on your toes with random fun news, warnings, and alerts. These pop-ups add an extra layer of excitement and unpredictability to the game, making each playthrough unique.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/04aa98a50231ce7085639dad2245ad86cb1804c2.png[/img]

[h1]Better UI[/h1]
We’ve revamped the main menu UI to include better descriptions and visuals of the location map. Now it’s easier than ever to navigate and understand the various options and settings available to you. Similarly, the campaign level menu has received a UI upgrade. Enhanced descriptions and a more intuitive layout ensure that you can jump into the action without any confusion. As well as an improved building menu UI for shadows, more items, slimmer and overall intuitive.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d9e412bdb0a212dd9166edc578cc88056dce6710.png[/img]

[h1]Unique Polyester Graphics[/h1]
This will make your floats look more smooth and visually appealing, adding to the overall immersion of the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/c2c86e5113e4646a136022b30f4f1a8d5caaa98f.png[/img]

[h1]New Camera Scene: Rotation[/h1]
We’ve added a fancy new camera rotation feature! This allows you to rotate the camera around your float, providing you with stunning new angles and perspectives.

Even when the game is paused, you can now rotate the camera around your float. This feature is perfect for taking a closer look at your work or planning your next move while on a break.

[h1]And much more!![/h1]
The full update log will be released when the update goes live, detailing all the new features, changes, and fixes. Development is ongoing, and we’re also working on blueprints, grouping, pulling tractors, adjusting cart lengths, decoratable generator cart, props for even more creative possibilities and much more! Expect this update to roll out in the coming weeks, and stay tuned for more updates!

Thank you for your continued support and enthusiasm. Let’s make Carnaval Simulator the best it can be!

notes.title: The Grand Expansion Update (1.1) - Dev Diary
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!! The biggest update Carnaval Simulator has yet received is still work in progress: [b]The Grand Expansion Update[/b] (1.1). This update will contain new content and a bunch of bug fixes (especially rotations making them user-friendly). The update includes an overall massive improvement of the game hence its name. All updates for Carnaval Simulator are heavily influenced by the community's wants and needs and are combined with the vision I have for the game. So if you have any wishes or suggestions, make sure to let us know on Discord! Without further ado, let's show what's to come in the upcoming update!

[h1]Fountain Fireworks[/h1]
Just like in real life, some floats both at day time and at night use fountain fireworks to impress its audience. The upcoming update will include 2 types of fountain fireworks: regular & large. The large one can only be placed once per float. These are high-level items, akin to other show elements such as smoke machines.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/de82c31d12c40b7bcbe83f859d878a7f5d239f23.png[/img]

[h1]Colorable lasers[/h1]
While adding new content is really fun, sometimes it's also crucial to return and update some of the existing items. The option to change the colors of lasers has been added, enhancing customization options for lights. More customizations for lights are in the planning stages.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/888116ab73c84eac421521ea35fa688fdb2fb602.png[/img]

[h1]New Smoke[/h1]
Speaking of smoke, smoke effects have received a massive graphical update, enhancing realism and interaction with colorful lights. In real-life, I love seeing the smoke being used in combination with colorful lights so of course I had to find a way to make this possible. It's far more realistic overal including the way it floats around.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/badf441bf8e8abcf11d7df80a1a917ee0dbc4d0b.png[/img]

Old smoke:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d88307b20e09506d72826a9b74277086c4943b91.png[/img]

[h1]Letters & Numbers[/h1]
A very much requested feature is the ability to add letters to your float. All the letters of the latin alphabet have been added. Now you can spell things out or use them in a very creative manner. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/0febc7daec22e1f56e898fcb80afedb0c0dead20.png[/img]
And of course, when I added the letters, why not add the numbers?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d30a6441f9d5d9867413ab12e3b5361a0a58e5e3.png[/img]

[h1]Confetti[/h1]
Players can now throw confetti for added interaction in first-person mode, providing an enjoyable and fun addition to gameplay. This fun little gimmick ended up to be way more enjoyable to play with than I expected. And yes, you can spam click to throw a lot of confetti.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/ed69992b4596c2a8e5fff0e855abb6e5e86f0dfa.png[/img]

[h1]New flags[/h1]
Additional flags representing major German Carnival cities will be included in the update.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/a187fe55d0884fb2ea6dbbde3f130c3dc4cb800f.png[/img]

[h1]Water[/h1]
Water has been added to Farmlands. Not a major feature, but I love how it turned out visually. I don't wanna say too much about the future, but let's say it's gonna be reused in some way or another ;)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/363ed6c7b89639358968b9412bda4d062e515168.png[/img]

[h1]And much more!![/h1]
The full update log will be released as soon as the update hits, featuring numerous additions, changes, and fixes. Currently, developement is focussed on the long promised customizable front cart as well as a revamped score system. Additionally, more characters and other props are being worked on for further creative possibilities. When will this update hit? It will take a few weeks to finalize the update. It is expected to be released around Easter, but it may arrive later in April. I will keep you guys up to date! 

Lastly, all promised features mentioned in the last anouncement are still on the table, except for the durability mechanic. We have bigger plans for this one in the next [b]Disco & Weather Update[/b] (1.2).

notes.title: Major Update 1.1.0 in Development!
notes.notes:
Howdy guys! It's been a bit since last post. I got really sick the past time and Carnaval took place. Now I have recovered for most part and I am happy to announce that work is being made on the next major update! For now on, larger updates will take place that will take some longer time to develop. I may still throw in some small updates after each one though but expect longer update times but in return you receive greater content. All updates will be of course completely free :)

I have made my general plans for the year all the way up to Carnaval 2025 for the game's official release. Great things are ahead of us, this will raise the game's quality massively. 

So what will be in this major update? Well I already made a post about the plans for Carnaval Simulator a while ago. Plans have changed in some ways though due to revisions, community feedback or it got added to the game already. 
 
Here's what to expect:
[list]
[*] Customizable front cart (finally hidding your tractor)
[*] Proper stretch mechanic -> stretch your props in certain ways
[*] Gravity score mechanic -> don't worry, this will not affect sandbox and it's only a score mechanic
[*] Durability mechanic, affected by the temperature
[*] A better value system for each prop
[*] Crew progression perks -> crew becomes more useful
[*] Honking in multiplayer
[*] Throwing confetti in first person
[*] More loading screens
[*] More camera controls
[*] More props -> currently I can promise a new character, the rest is a secret
[/list]

Besides these new features, I will always try to fix bugs whenever I can. I am really grateful to all people reporting these bugs. They all get looked at.

Old promises that have been altered:
[list]
[*] Spectator camera -> already added in update
[*] Rearrangement of the mod structure -> moved to the future
[*] More modable options -> moved to the future
[*] Better learning curve / more balanced game -> already dealt with but changes may still occur all through out development
[/list]

I will keep you guys up to date on the progress. I cannot provide an exact release date but this information will follow. Smaller additions like a button to enable all rotations in build mode may be added too but I will let you guys know about this as the update progresses. I hope you guys have a wonderful weekend, we will see each other next time. Ciao!

notes.title: Merry Christmas!! Dev Diary & Roadmap to Release Jan 2024
notes.notes:
Greetings folks! First of all, the development of Carnaval Simulator is still on-going. I have been seeing huge progress which is key to its release in January 2024. Due to the size of this dev diary I will be splitting this up in different parts (next dev diary in early January). Let's share this dev diary and reveal the roadmap for 2024, so what are my plans for the future? What is already finished? How's the development going? This is gonna be a long one so let's get started!

[h1]Build Maps[/h1]
Let's start with build maps. Within Carnaval Simulator, you create your parade float on your building terrain. This is a separate map from the city. In real life, these parade floats are typically made in rural and industrial areas. Therefore I have tried to make various maps distinctly different from each other yet sharing this common real life fact. At release there will be 3 different maps: Denlake Valley (a forest map), Farmlands and Industrial Area. These maps are unlocked when you level up. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/ab048e27ba01997195ff24a5967af79961392f8f.png[/img]

It's mostly cosmetic for the sake of immersion except for the resource locations scattered around the map. Resources are mostly given at the start of each game or rewarded by winning parades but a small bonus can be found within the map itself. Additionally one may also find collectables around all maps. They aren't visible in the camera mode so they are harder to spot! Finding them rewards you with fun facts about the real life Carnival celebration. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/e3246723eb6430e08d3117cac735aebdb5d6353a.png[/img]

[h1]City Map[/h1]
As mentioned before, there's a separate map for the city in which the actual parade takes place in. Also in this map you will be able to find collectables. In singleplayer this is mostly the visual presentation of your float and you will get your results at the end. In multiplayer this scene lets the players vote for each float that comes around. For release, it's my goal to fully finish the map with all its important details. In the future I wanna add more maps for more variety. They will be parodies of real life towns which are meaningful to the real life celebration and who knows, we may travel around the world? Lastly, the amount of build maps (3) are currently efficient for the end product, but they may receive small visual updates in the future

[h1]Campaign Levels[/h1]
An important gamemode in Carnaval Simulator is the campaign mode (singleplayer). These are all unique levels that provide the player with unique challenges. Examples of these levels are: being very tight on time so you will have to create your float very rapidly, all props being built without color which teaches you how to color the props (they give you extra points for doing so), specific themes giving you the points necessary to win, starting without any resources but you will have to find them scattered around the map in first person mode and much more! They essentially help you teach the game further. There's a tutorial in game which teaches you the very basics but this will help you understand the mechanics more deeply. I think it's way more fun to learn from these challenges. Above all, they give you special EXP when you complete a level as well as unlocking the next level. 

For release I will be tweaking the existing campaign levels and create some new ones as new mechanics are being developed (such as the limited stock mechanic).

[h1]Steam Workshop[/h1]
Mod support is crucial to extending the lifespan of games like Carnaval Simulator for creating more unique creations and engaging challenges. Therefore, I have decided to prioritize mod support so users can upload and download custom content very easily. Right now users may share custom props, custom music and custom campaign levels. After downloading them you will only have to open the game to see the custom content appear. This will further extend the possibilities to user's creations.

Additionally, there's an option to share your own creations as you can see in the workshop. Your very own floats can be shared, similar how you may share a world or map in other games. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/e8e8f30a8d48ae21b963c09d49ea71f7c7d5ee89.png[/img]

The way you create these mods can be examined through the examples on the Steam Workshop. But I may add a simple guide on [url=https://carnavalsim.nl/]Carnaval Simulator's website[/url] as well. Right now the only limitation is that you can't make 1 main mod that adds music, props etc. all together. You will have to create separate mods for this. After its release I will restructure the mod system so you will be able to create everything in 1 mod and perhaps more customization options as the features of this game will grow. I am curious what people will create!

[h1]Score System[/h1]
When playing single player or with very few players you may let the AI decide which float gains the most votes. There are various categories to gain points from:
[list]
[*] Float rating
[*] Excitement rating
[*] Height rating
[*] Music rating
[*] Light rating
[*] Bonus rating
[/list]
Right now the player will be able to view how well they did in a specific category so they can reflect and construct an even more impressive float! A very difficult aspect to this was the balance between creative freedom vs interesting gameplay mechanics. I have tried to provide the player with as much creative freedom as possible within certain constraints. Each campaign level additionally offers different challenges but also non-campaign modes generate specific traits & themes that provide the player with additional points based on the world's seed. This system will receive constant updates as the game develops so expect changes in future updates! I will not go deeper into how these points are granted since it is ultimately the jury's decision.

[h1]Crew Mechanics & Limited Stocks[/h1]
A very much requested feature for this game is the ability to add crew members. I essentially turned the citizens from the town map into crew members and added mechanics around them. I created limited stocks for certain items and integrated this with the staff members as well. The size of your float determines how many you assign to your crew. They aren't necessary however but they do help you with your excitement rating which is given for the interactions between your float and the crowd. 

They have the same simplistic look as the citizens in the city for the sake of consistency. This is intentional so we can add lots of citizens for better performance. In the future, I may update the graphical look of them but for now it's not a priority. They perform random dances, and their outfits are also randomly generated (although you can customize them)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/739ebba743dffab3eea4cc099d22b1b1a62b3503.png[/img]

In the future I would like to expand on this mechanic for more depth to the game. Expect more options to interact with your crew in future updates! 

[h1]Achievements[/h1]
For now there are 11 achievements in the game. This perfectly matches another system I have built which keeps track of various statistics based on your gameplay, such as the number of props you have placed or the amount of floats you have built. In the future we may add more achievements but that's low priority for now.
